description: Backblaze Drive Stats is a public dataset of the health and failures of the storage drives running in the data centres of the cloud storage company Backblaze, published since 2013. Every day Backblaze records a snapshot of each operational drive, with its model, serial number, capacity, whether it failed that day and the S.M.A.R.T. self-monitoring attributes it reports, such as power-on hours, temperature, reallocated and pending bad sectors and error counts. Each quarter the company publishes the new data and a report of annualised failure rates by drive model and manufacturer (HGST, Seagate, Toshiba and Western Digital), and yearly and lifetime summaries. The first quarter of 2026 snapshot covers 341,263 drives. The data have been used widely in academic research on predicting disk failures and on how failure rates change with age and temperature. Coverage: Backblaze data centres in the United States and Europe, 2013 to present. Format and access: quarterly ZIP archives of daily CSV files, about 1 to 1.3 GB compressed each, free; users must cite Backblaze and may not sell the data itself. Caveats: one operator's fleet and workload, mostly consumer and enterprise hard drives in similar enclosures; S.M.A.R.T. fields differ between models. Simulation uses: component failure and ageing models for data-centre reliability studies, spare parts planning and calibration of failure predictors. Related records: the Cloud Uptime Archive and Uptime Institute outage analysis cover service-level failures.
